outcome: The density hypothesis is still open. No event in the window proves N(σ,T) ≪ T^(2(1−σ)+ε) on any new range of σ: Guth–Maynard (arXiv May 2024; Annals 2026) lowered the best known supremum of the zero-density exponent from 12/5 to 30/13, still above the density hypothesis's 2; the widest unconditional range remains Bourgain's (2000, σ ≥ 25/32). In-window claims near the topic are an OpenAI zero-free half-plane (Re s > 7/8, unreviewed), a withdrawn RH claim, a lecture abstract whose scope is ambiguous, and a Claude-credited result on the proportion of zeros on the critical line that is a different quantity.
problem_asks: Statement as given to me: 'The density hypothesis for zeroes of the Riemann zeta function' (the bullet gives no further wording). The standard form the bullet names, taken from the literature (Wikipedia's Lindelöf-hypothesis article, density hypothesis subsection, reached via the redirect; and the zero-density papers opened below): for σ real and T ≥ 2, let N(σ,T) = number of zeros ρ = β+iγ of ζ with β ≥ σ and 0 < γ ≤ T. The problem asks for N(σ,T) ≪_ε T^(2(1−σ)+ε) for every ε > 0. Parts: (a) every σ in [1/2,1]; the content is the open range 1/2 < σ < 1, since at σ = 1/2 the bound T^(1+ε) is trivial from the Riemann–von Mangoldt count; (b) uniformity in T; (c) the ε-loss in the exponent (the literature also states a sharper log-power form, c·T^(2(1−σ))·(log T)^A). Equivalent exponent form: A(σ) ≤ 2 for all σ in [1/2,1], where N(σ,T) = T^(A(σ)(1−σ)+o(1)). Parent context (not a sub-question): the Lindelöf hypothesis implies this (Ingham 1937), but the converse is not asked.

events.what_happened: Halász and Turán proved the density hypothesis unconditionally in a narrow fixed strip 1 − c < Re s < 1 with a small, unspecified effective constant c. Stated in the abstract of Pintz's Rényi Institute lecture (opened) and in Pintz's 2022 and 2023 papers (search summaries). The year 1969 is my background recollection of the Halász–Turán paper and was not confirmed in any source I opened, so the date is provisional.
events.delivers: The density hypothesis (exponent 2) for σ in a narrow strip 1 − c < σ < 1 with small unspecified c; nothing for σ near 1/2.
events.remains: All of the density hypothesis for 1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 1 − c.
events.direction: Consistent with the density hypothesis; proves it in a strip near Re s = 1.

events.what_happened: Ingham (1937) showed conditionally that the Lindelöf hypothesis implies the density hypothesis: if ζ(1/2+it) ≪ t^(c+ε) then N(σ,T) ≪ T^((2+4c)(1−σ))(log T)^5, which at c = 0 gives the density hypothesis. Source: a search summary of the Ingham 1937 bound (the 1937 paper itself was not opened). A later alternative proof is attributed to Turán (1954) in the same search summary.
events.delivers: Conditional on the Lindelöf hypothesis (the parent problem), the density hypothesis for all σ.
events.remains: Unconditionally, the whole density hypothesis; the parent is itself open.
events.direction: Parent implies child under an extra hypothesis; does not settle the child.

events.what_happened: Ingham (1940): unconditional N(σ,T) ≪ T^(3(1−σ)/(2−σ)) log^5 T for 1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 1, i.e. A(σ) = 3/(2−σ). Stated in the density hypothesis subsection of Wikipedia (opened) and in search summaries of Baluyot's CNTA XV slides (slides not readable on fetch). The 1940 paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: A(σ) = 3/(2−σ). This exceeds 2 for every σ in (1/2, 1], so it gives the density hypothesis at no σ > 1/2; it is the baseline that later work improves for σ ≤ 7/10.
events.remains: The density hypothesis for all σ in (1/2, 1].
events.direction: Partial bound on the exponent; does not reach the density hypothesis's exponent 2 for any σ > 1/2.

events.what_happened: Montgomery (1971): zero-density exponent A ≤ 2/σ for 4/5 ≤ σ ≤ 1 (search summary of Baluyot's slides, not readable on fetch). Chen–Debruyne–Vindas, arXiv:2310.14797, instead attributes to Montgomery the density hypothesis for σ ≥ 9/10 (opened). Range conflict recorded in disputes.
events.delivers: The density hypothesis for σ in [4/5, 1] (or [9/10, 1] per the other source); fully inside the later Bourgain range.
events.remains: The density hypothesis for 1/2 < σ < 4/5 (or 9/10).
events.direction: Confirms the density hypothesis near σ = 1 only.

events.what_happened: Huxley: N(σ,T) ≪ T^(3(1−σ)/(3σ−1)) log^44 T for 3/4 ≤ σ ≤ 1, i.e. A(σ) = 3/(3σ−1); combined with Ingham's bound this gives the sup exponent 12/5 for 1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 1. Wikipedia (opened) dates it Huxley (1971); search summaries date it 1972. Year conflict recorded in disputes. Original paper not opened.
events.delivers: A(σ) ≤ 3/(3σ−1) for 3/4 ≤ σ ≤ 1. This is ≤ 2 only for σ ≥ 5/6, so the density hypothesis on [5/6, 1] by this bound alone; the sup over [1/2,1] is 12/5 (with Ingham).
events.remains: The density hypothesis for 1/2 < σ < 5/6 by this bound.
events.direction: Improves the exponent; reaches the density hypothesis only near σ = 1.

events.what_happened: Jutila (1977): density hypothesis (A ≤ 2) for 11/14 ≤ σ ≤ 1 for ζ, per a search summary of Baluyot's slides (not readable on fetch). Search summary also mentions an earlier Jutila (1972) density theorem for L-functions with a real character.
events.delivers: The density hypothesis for σ in [11/14, 1].
events.remains: The density hypothesis for 1/2 < σ < 11/14; the range 25/32 ≤ σ < 11/14 is covered by Bourgain (2000) below.
events.direction: Confirms the density hypothesis for σ near 1.

events.what_happened: Bourgain (2000), 'On large values estimates for Dirichlet polynomials and the density hypothesis for the Riemann zeta function', Internat. Math. Res. Notices 2000 no. 3, pp. 133–146. The bibliographic record came from a search result; the paper itself was not opened. Stated (search summaries and the Rényi lecture abstract) as establishing the density hypothesis for σ ≥ 25/32 (equivalently Re s > 0.78; the Rényi abstract says 'for any c<0.22'), which the Rényi abstract calls the current record.
events.delivers: The density hypothesis for 25/32 ≤ σ ≤ 1 (for ζ). This is the widest unconditional range for the density hypothesis that I found in any source through October 2026.
events.remains: The density hypothesis for 1/2 < σ < 25/32.
events.doubts: The original paper was not read; the 25/32 threshold rests on secondary citations (search summaries and the Rényi abstract).
events.direction: Confirms the density hypothesis on a range near σ = 1.

events.what_happened: Yuanyou Cheng posted arXiv:0810.2103 on 12 Oct 2008 as 'Proof of the Density Hypothesis' (v1). v2 (28 Oct 2008) is titled 'A Proof for the Density Hypothesis' and states 'we give a proof for the density hypothesis'. v14 (4 Jun 2021, the version fetched) is titled 'Proof of the strong Density Hypothesis' and gives N(λ,T) ≤ 8.734 log T for 1/2 < λ < 1 and T ≥ 2445999554999, claiming 'a proof of the density hypothesis'. v15 (15 Jun 2021) was withdrawn by arXiv administrators 'due to disputed authorship'. A search snippet described a later version with coauthors Albeverio, Graham, Graham and Pomerance and a bound of 5.423 log T; I could not reconcile this with the v14 text I fetched. v3 to v13 (2008–2012) were not individually opened.
events.revisions: v1 12 Oct 2008 (Proof of the Density Hypothesis); v2 28 Oct 2008 (A Proof for the Density Hypothesis); v3–v13 2008–2012 (not individually opened; v14 comment says revised 3 Aug 2010, final version 26 Nov 2012, submitted to J. Number Theory); v14 4 Jun 2021 (strong form, bound 8.734 log T); v15 15 Jun 2021 withdrawn by arXiv admin.
events.delivers: Claims the full density hypothesis, and in its strong form N(λ,T) ≤ 8.734 log T for 1/2 < λ < 1, T ≥ 2445999554999. If correct, this settles the whole problem; the claimed bound is logarithmic, stronger than the statement's T^ε form.
events.remains: Nothing, if the claim were correct; but the version carrying the claim was withdrawn.
events.doubts: (1) Withdrawn by arXiv administrators in June 2021 'due to disputed authorship' (v15). (2) Author list changes between versions (v14 lists Cheng alone; a search snippet gives coauthors). (3) Two different bounds appear (8.734 log T in v14; 5.423 log T in a version seen only in a search snippet). (4) No peer-reviewed publication and no expert engagement found; Pintz (2023) and the 2025 Rényi abstract both still treat the density hypothesis as open.

withdrawn.what: v15 withdrawn by arXiv administrators; arXiv comment: 'This submission has been withdrawn by arXiv administrators due to disputed authorship.'

events.direction: Claims to prove the density hypothesis in full, i.e. cuts for the conjecture; withdrawn.
people: Sergio Albeverio (in a search snippet only)

events.what_happened: János Pintz, 'A remark on density theorems for Riemann's zeta-function', arXiv:2310.04544 (submitted 30 Sep 2023), published in Science China Mathematics 66 (2023), pp. 2795–2802 (DOI 10.1007/s11425-023-2215-7, from search results, not opened). Gives a simpler proof of known zero-density estimates 'sufficiently strong to break the density hypothesis in a nontrivial part of the critical strip' (arXiv abstract, opened). A search summary of the abstract says 'for Re s > 7/8'; the abstract as fetched does not state the range.
events.delivers: Unconditional zero-density bounds on ζ that are sharper than the density hypothesis's 2(1−σ) in part of the strip near Re s = 1 (the search summary says Re s > 7/8, which lies inside Bourgain's range). Does not extend the density hypothesis to any new range of σ.
events.remains: The density hypothesis for 1/2 < σ < 25/32 and whatever part of [25/32,1] is not covered.

checked_by.what_they_did: published the paper (vol. 66, 2023, pp. 2795–2802); acceptance and editorial process not examined

events.doubts: The range of the sharper bound is stated differently in the arXiv abstract ('a nontrivial part of the critical strip') and in a search summary ('Re s > 7/8'); the full text was not read.
events.direction: Strengthens zero-density estimates on ζ in a region near σ = 1; a partial result on the density hypothesis, not a proof of it.

events.what_happened: Bin Chen, Gregory Debruyne, Jasson Vindas, 'On the density hypothesis for L-functions associated with holomorphic cusp forms', arXiv:2310.14797, first submitted 10 Oct 2023 and revised 26 Mar 2024; published in Rev. Mat. Iberoam. 40 (2024) (per search). Proves N_f(σ,T) ≪ T^(2(1−σ)+ε) for σ ≥ 1407/1601 for L-functions of holomorphic cusp eigenforms, improving Ivić's σ ≥ 53/60. Uses mixed moment estimates for ζ as an input.
events.revisions: v1 10 Oct 2023; v2 revised 26 Mar 2024 (in the window; content of revision not checked).
events.delivers: The density hypothesis for L-functions of cusp forms, for σ ≥ 1407/1601. Concerns cusp-form L-functions, not ζ itself, so it is an analogue of the problem.
events.remains: For ζ itself, nothing new from this paper.
events.direction: Analogue: density hypothesis for a different family; confirms it there on a range near σ = 1.

events.what_happened: Kaisa Matomäki and Joni Teräväinen, 'A note on zero density results implying large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials', arXiv:2403.13157, submitted 19 Mar 2024 (single version, opened). Shows that zero-density estimates for ζ imply large-value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials, the reverse of the usual implication.
events.delivers: A link between zero-density estimates and large values of Dirichlet polynomials. It establishes no new bound on N(σ,T) and says nothing about the exponent for the density hypothesis.
events.remains: The whole density hypothesis.
events.time_since_posted: about 2.6 years; no public engagement found in searches
events.direction: Neighbouring; does not bear on the density hypothesis's exponent.

events.what_happened: Larry Guth and James Maynard, 'New large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials', arXiv:2405.20552 (v1 submitted 31 May 2024; v2 submitted 7 Apr 2026). Theorem 1.2 (opened, HTML v2): N(σ,T) ≤ T^(15(1−σ)/(3+5σ)+o(1)). Combined with Ingham's estimate for σ ≤ 7/10 this gives N(σ,T) ≤ T^(30(1−σ)/13+o(1)) (the paper's stated consequence; the abstract states the 30(1−σ)/13 form). Published in Annals of Mathematics vol. 203 (2026), no. 2, pp. 623–675, online 1 March 2026 (opened). The paper does not mention the density hypothesis, A(σ) or a supremum; it says 30/13 improves on Huxley's 12/5.
events.revisions: v1 31 May 2024; v2 7 Apr 2026 (the abstract page does not describe changes); Annals version online 1 Mar 2026 (vol. 203, issue 2) — the Annals online date precedes arXiv v2.
events.delivers: In the notation A(σ): A(σ) ≤ 15/(3+5σ) for σ ≥ 7/10 and Ingham's 3/(2−σ) below, so sup over σ of A(σ) is 30/13 (attained at σ = 7/10), replacing 12/5. Since 30/13 > 2, this does not give the density hypothesis at any σ ≤ 9/10 (where A(σ) > 2); the density hypothesis's range is unchanged (Bourgain's σ ≥ 25/32 remains the widest). It moves the sup exponent, which is a quantity the density hypothesis's A(σ) ≤ 2 bounds, but does not reach 2.
events.remains: The density hypothesis for 1/2 < σ < 25/32 entirely, and for σ in [25/32, 9/10) it is covered only by earlier work; the sup exponent is 30/13 > 2.

checked_by.who: Annals of Mathematics editors and referees (names not published on the page)
checked_by.what_they_did: accepted and published the paper, vol. 203 (2026), issue 2, pp. 623–675, online 1 Mar 2026

events.time_since_posted: about 2.4 years since v1 (May 2024 to Oct 2026)
events.doubts: (1) A self-published critique by José Miguel Robles Leyton (Preprints.org, 14 Jul 2025, DOI 10.20944/preprints202507.1068.v1; 0 reviews on prereview.org) says it identifies four 'expository gaps' and supplies derivations, including of the 30(1−σ)/13 exponent as a harmonic mean of the Ingham and Guth–Maynard bounds. Its abstract does not say the main result is wrong; the four gaps were not checked here. (2) A search summary of a MATRIX 2024 talk slide gives 5/9 at σ = 3/4 where the paper's formula gives 15/26; probably a normalisation difference, not checked. (3) v2 (April 2026) changes are not stated.
events.direction: Lowers the sup of the zero-density exponent from 12/5 to 30/13; the density hypothesis needs 2, so it does not cut for or against the conjecture; it moves a related quantity without crossing the threshold.

events.what_happened: Chiara Bellotti, 'An explicit log-free zero density estimate for the Riemann zeta-function', arXiv:2405.12545, v1 21 May 2024, v2 25 May 2024 (opened). Explicit log-free bound N(σ,T) ≤ A·T^(B(1−σ)) for ζ, claimed sharpest known explicit for σ in [α0, 1] with 0.985 ≤ α0 ≤ 0.9927 and 3·10^12 < T ≤ exp(6.7·10^12). The abstract does not state A or B.
events.delivers: Explicit-constant zero-density bound for ζ, only for σ in [α0, 1] near 1, where the density hypothesis is already known from Bourgain (σ ≥ 25/32). Whether its exponent B is ≤ 2 is not stated in the abstract.
events.remains: The density hypothesis for 1/2 < σ < α0, and the statement's ε-form without explicit constants for all T.
events.time_since_posted: about 2.4 years; no public engagement found in searches
events.direction: Neighbouring; a sharper explicit bound in a region already covered.

events.what_happened: Chiara Bellotti and Peng-Jie Wong, 'Improved estimates for the argument and zero-counting function of the Riemann zeta-function', arXiv:2412.15470, v1 20 Dec 2024, v2 7 Jul 2025 (opened). Explicit error bound for N(T), the count of zeros with 0 < γ ≤ T; no zero-density exponent for N(σ,T).
events.delivers: Bounds the total zero count N(T), not N(σ,T) with σ > 1/2. Does not bear on the density hypothesis.
events.remains: The whole density hypothesis.
events.time_since_posted: about 1.8 years; no public engagement found in searches
events.direction: Neighbouring; different quantity.

events.what_happened: Bin Chen, Vishal Gupta, Yung Chi Li, 'Large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials, and the density of zeros of Dirichlet L-functions', arXiv:2507.08296, v1 11 Jul 2025, v2 27 Jul 2026 (opened). Bound for the sum over characters mod q of the zero count: Σ_χ N(σ,T,χ) ≪ (qT)^(7(1−σ)/3+ε), exponent 7/3, 'improves upon Huxley's earlier exponent of 12/5' for that family; built by adapting the Guth–Maynard method. A search summary said v1 listed Bin Chen alone; the current page lists three authors.
events.revisions: v1 11 Jul 2025; v2 27 Jul 2026 (changes not read).
events.delivers: A zero-density bound for the family of Dirichlet L-functions mod q, exponent 7/3. The abstract does not state the modulus-1 (zeta) case, though a search summary says it recovers Guth–Maynard there (not verified). Family-level, not ζ; a density-hypothesis analogue for L-functions would need exponent 2, and 7/3 > 2.
events.remains: The density hypothesis for ζ, and for L-functions in the family (exponent 2).
events.doubts: Author list differs between a search summary (Bin Chen alone, v1) and the current page (three authors); the page says the result is an adaptation of the Guth–Maynard method.
events.direction: Analogue (family of Dirichlet L-functions); exponent above the density hypothesis's 2.

events.what_happened: Daniel A. Goldston and Ade Irma Suriajaya, 'Zeta Zeros on the Critical Line', arXiv:2511.20059, v1 25 Nov 2025, v2 5 Feb 2026 (abstract opened). Says that removing RH from Montgomery's 1973 simple-zero argument would also give at least 2/3 of zeros simple and on the critical line. It is conditional on the removal.
events.delivers: A conditional statement about the proportion of simple zeros on the line. Concerns a different quantity; no zero-density or N(σ,T) claim.
events.remains: The whole density hypothesis (outside scope).
events.doubts: Conditional; the search summary says a version under a narrow-region assumption exists; full text not read.
events.direction: Different question (proportion on the line), conditional.

events.what_happened: José Miguel Robles Leyton (listed as 'Jose Robles' on the page), 'Spectral Analysis of Expository Gaps in New Large Value Estimates for Dirichlet Polynomials: Rigorous Solutions and Methodological Frameworks', Preprints.org DOI 10.20944/preprints202507.1068.v1, posted 14 Jul 2025 (abstract opened via prereview.org; the Preprints.org PDF returned HTTP 403). Claims to analyse four expository gaps in Guth–Maynard and to give a derivation of their exponent 30(1−σ)/13 as a harmonic mean of the Ingham and Guth–Maynard bounds. Says its method is 'a hybrid methodology combining traditional mathematical analysis with artificial intelligence techniques'.
events.delivers: Nothing on the density hypothesis; a critique of the exposition of Guth–Maynard's zero-density result.
events.remains: The whole density hypothesis.
events.doubts: Self-published and unreviewed; the four gaps are not identified in the abstract, and no check of their validity was made here.
events.direction: Neutral on the density hypothesis; a claim about the exposition of a related result.

events.what_happened: János Pintz, Rényi Institute number theory seminar lecture 'On the density hypothesis for Riemann's zeta-function', 11 Nov 2025 (Nagyterem and Zoom; abstract opened). The abstract says the lecture 'will prove the density hypothesis using only general complex function theory and Riemann's functional equation', without subconvexity bounds on the critical line, Turán's method or the large sieve, 'but it will use Halász's idea'. The same abstract says Halász and Turán proved the hypothesis 'in a narrow strip near Re s = 1' and that Bourgain's 2000 result, the current record, covers Re s > 0.78. No preprint, notes or video were found.
events.delivers: Unclear from the abstract. Read literally, a new proof of the full density hypothesis by elementary methods; read alongside its own history paragraph, possibly a new proof of the narrow-strip (Halász–Turán) density theorem. The record cannot decide between these readings.
events.remains: Depends on the reading: either the density hypothesis outside the narrow strip (if the full claim holds) or nothing beyond Halász–Turán (if the strip reading holds).
events.time_since_posted: about 11 months; no notes, video or preprint found
events.doubts: Only a seminar abstract exists; the scope sentence is ambiguous between the full density hypothesis and the narrow-strip theorem; no write-up found.
events.direction: Possibly a proof of the density hypothesis; the abstract does not say how far it reaches.

events.what_happened: Yunwei Bai, 'Analysis of the Riemann Zeta Function via Recursive Taylor Expansions', arXiv preprint v1 on 5 Mar 2026 (opened). Claims 'an unconditional proof that non-trivial zeros of the Riemann Zeta function must lie strictly on the critical line', i.e. the Riemann Hypothesis. v2 on 10 Mar 2026 is a 1 KB stub; the author withdrew the paper, with comment 'This copy contains a few problems identified by the author, and should be withdrawn promptly'.
events.revisions: v1 5 Mar 2026; v2 10 Mar 2026 (withdrawn by author, 1 KB)
events.delivers: If correct, the Riemann Hypothesis, which implies the density hypothesis for every σ > 1/2 (no zeros off the line gives N(σ,T) = 0). Withdrawn, so it establishes nothing.
events.remains: The whole density hypothesis, as far as this paper's status goes.
events.doubts: Withdrawn by the author, who says the copy 'contains a few problems identified by the author'; no review found.

withdrawn.what: v2 withdrawn by the author; comment: 'This copy contains a few problems identified by the author, and should be withdrawn promptly'

events.direction: Would cut for the density hypothesis (it implies it); withdrawn.

events.what_happened: Vishal Gupta (Oxford), 'Lindelöf hypothesis and zero density estimates', Junior Number Theory Seminar, Oxford, 25 May 2026 (page opened). Proves, conditional on the Lindelöf hypothesis, a new upper bound on N(σ,T) of the form T^(exponent(σ)+o(1)), improving the Lindelöf-conditional exponent 2(1−σ), 'particularly for σ near 3/4'. The exponent is not shown on the page. No write-up found in the searches.
events.delivers: Conditional on the Lindelöf hypothesis (the parent), a zero-density bound with exponent below the density hypothesis's 2(1−σ) near σ = 3/4. Does not settle the density hypothesis, which the Lindelöf hypothesis already implies under that assumption.
events.remains: The unconditional density hypothesis.
events.doubts: Seminar abstract only; the exponent was seen in a search summary (4(5−6σ)/(3(3−2σ))) but not on the page itself.
events.direction: Conditional improvement of the density exponent; no unconditional movement.

The post says it makes no claim about the density hypothesis or about zero-density estimates N(σ,T). The post names Brian Conrey and Dan Goldston as external experts who 'generously examined the paper on short notice'.

events.delivers: A lower bound on the proportion of nontrivial zeros of ζ on the line (41.6% to 67.2%); the paper with it also claims simple and distinct zero proportions. This is a different quantity from N(σ,T) for σ > 1/2, so it does not bear on the density hypothesis's bound.

events.what_happened: Levent Alpöge and Ralph Furman, 'More than two thirds of the zeta zeros are simple and on the critical line', arXiv:2608.13637, v1 13 Aug 2026, v2 19 Aug 2026 (abstract page and HTML v2 opened; the PDF was not readable). events.what_happened: Catherine Cossaboom, 'Zero density estimates for GL_2 automorphic L-functions', arXiv:2609.27715, v1 23 Sep 2026 (only version; abstract page opened). Gives N_π(σ,T) ≪ T^((5/2)(1−σ)+o(1)) for cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_2, extending the Guth–Maynard method.
events.delivers: A zero-density bound for GL_2 automorphic L-functions with exponent 5/2 (above the density hypothesis's 2 for the GL_2 analogue). Not ζ; not the density hypothesis.
events.remains: The density hypothesis for ζ and its analogues.
events.doubts: Abstract only; the full text not read.
events.direction: Analogue for a different family; exponent above 2.

events.what_happened: OpenAI released 'openai/math' on GitHub, containing manuscripts from 'an internal OpenAI model' (GitHub page opened; the page says 719 manuscripts in 372 families; secondary coverage says 722). Among these: 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane Re s > 7/8' (main manuscript, dated 30 Sep 2026 per a search summary; claims all Dirichlet L-functions, Hecke L-functions over Q(√−3) and ζ have no zeros with Re s > 7/8, principal pole at s = 1 allowed; the Lean scope note says the 7/8 statement is formalised for ζ, Dirichlet and Hecke L-functions); and a companion with a different proof giving a zero-free half-plane Re s > 11/12 for all Dirichlet L-functions including ζ (not Lean-formalised per Emergent Mind). The GitHub page's zeta writeup for 11/12 says it was human edited. Public release date 6 Oct 2026 per news coverage (postcutoff); manuscripts dated 30 Sep to 5 Oct 2026 (Emergent Mind).
events.revisions: Manuscripts dated 30 Sep to 5 Oct 2026 (Emergent Mind); public repository release reported 6 Oct 2026 (news); later repository changes not tracked.
events.delivers: For ζ: zero-free half-plane Re s > 7/8 (main manuscript) or Re s > 11/12 (companion). Either gives N(σ,T) = 0 for σ above the bound, which satisfies the density hypothesis for those σ, but Bourgain (2000) already gives the density hypothesis from σ ≥ 25/32, so no new range of σ is reached. The result is a fixed zero-free half-plane, far stronger than the T-dependent zero-free regions I know of (background judgement, not from a source).
events.remains: The density hypothesis for 1/2 < σ < 7/8 (or 11/12); those ranges are covered in part by earlier work only up to 25/32.

events.what_happened: Baiying Liu, 'Slightly improved zero-free half-planes for the quasi-Riemann hypothesis', arXiv:2610.12234, v1 8 Oct 2026 (abstract page opened). Says the OpenAI 7/8 result (which it cites as 'given by OpenAI') is slightly improved by varying the parameters b and ℓ, to B_r = 34999/40000 and B_new = (1507 − 2√921)/1653 ≈ 0.874957, for finite-order Hecke L-functions over Q(√−3) with transfer to Dirichlet L-functions. Cites a Lean formalisation.

events.remains: The density hypothesis for 1/2 < σ < about 0.875.

events.what_happened: Kristian Muri Knausgård, 'More than 83.9% of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are distinct and more than 67.35% are simple and on the critical line', arXiv:2610.08965, submitted 6 Oct 2026, one version (abstract page opened). Improves two of Lamzouri's estimates (88.93% simple-or-on-line; average 83.67%). The abstract says 'This work is an experiment in AI-assisted mathematical research' and that the proofs are formalised in Lean 4 with three axioms beyond Mathlib, each recording a search program.
events.delivers: Improved proportion bounds (distinct zeros ≥ 0.83900; simple zeros on the line ≥ 0.67353). Not the density hypothesis; the density hypothesis is not mentioned.
events.remains: The density hypothesis in full.

disputes.summary: Authorship of the Alpöge–Furman argument: the arXiv paper lists Alpöge and Furman as authors, but its opening note says 'discovered and written by Claude' and that the listed authors verified it. Lamzouri's abstract likewise credits the argument to 'an internal research version of Claude'. Not resolved here.

The OpenAI zero-free claim for ζ: the main manuscript states 7/8 for all Dirichlet L-functions, Hecke L-functions over Q(√−3) and ζ; the companion states 11/12 for all Dirichlet L-functions including ζ. News coverage gives 7/8 as the zeta bound; the GitHub page gives 11/12 for the zeta writeup. Manuscript counts also differ (719 on GitHub, 722 in news).

Pintz (2023): the arXiv abstract says the estimates break the density hypothesis 'in a nontrivial part of the critical strip'; a search summary of the same abstract says 'for Re s > 7/8'. The full text was not read.

Pintz's 2025 Rényi lecture abstract says it 'will prove the density hypothesis', but the same abstract describes the known Halász–Turán result as valid in 'a narrow strip near Re s = 1' and gives Bourgain as the record. Whether the lecture claims the full density hypothesis or only a strip result is not settled by the abstract.

Cheng's arXiv:0810.2103: author lists differ between versions (v14 lists Cheng alone; a search snippet lists Albeverio, Graham, Graham and Pomerance); arXiv admin note says 'author list truncated due to disputed authorship'; the bound is 8.734 log T in v14 and 5.423 log T in a version seen only in a snippet.

Chen–Gupta–Li (arXiv:2507.08296): a search summary says v1 listed Bin Chen alone; the current abstract page lists three authors (v2 revised 27 Jul 2026). A seminar abstract also describes a joint Gupta–Li adaptation.
Montgomery's density-hypothesis range: 4/5 ≤ σ ≤ 1 (search summary of Baluyot's slides) versus σ ≥ 9/10 (Chen–Debruyne–Vindas, arXiv:2310.14797).
Huxley's 3/(3σ−1) bound is dated 1971 by Wikipedia's density hypothesis subsection and 1972 by search summaries.

Claude's proportion bound (Anthropic, 10 Aug 2026; arXiv 13 Aug 2026) and the Lamzouri and Knausgård follow-ups (Sep–Oct 2026): the follow-ups improve or reprove the same proportion bound. Credit is for the research team's order of events, not a dispute, but the Lamzouri and Knausgård abstracts name the Claude argument as prior work.

summary: The density hypothesis (A(σ) ≤ 2 for 1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 1; N(σ,T) ≪ T^(2(1−σ)+ε)) is open as far as I can establish. Historically: the Lindelöf hypothesis implies it (Ingham 1937); Ingham 1940 and Huxley 1972 gave exponents above 2 in the range that matters; Montgomery 1971 and Jutila 1977 proved it near σ = 1; Bourgain 2000 (IMRN) is the widest unconditional range I found, σ ≥ 25/32; Halász–Turán proved it in a narrow strip near Re s = 1. Cheng's 2008 arXiv preprints claimed a full proof; the version carrying the strong claim was withdrawn by arXiv admin in 2021 for disputed authorship, and no expert engagement was found. The main in-window change to the zero-density exponent is Guth–Maynard (arXiv 31 May 2024; Annals 2026): with Ingham's bound it gives a sup exponent of 30/13 (at σ = 7/10), down from Huxley's 12/5, but 30/13 > 2 and the new bound is above the density hypothesis's exponent for every σ < 9/10, so it extends no range of the density hypothesis. Earlier work by Pintz (2023) and Chen–Debruyne–Vindas (2023, cusp forms) is in the same neighbourhood. In-window claims that touch the statement are: an OpenAI zero-free half-plane for ζ (Re s > 7/8 in the main manuscript, Re s > 11/12 in a companion; released 6 Oct 2026, not peer reviewed; a fixed zero-free half-plane gives N(σ,T) = 0 above the bound, which satisfies the density hypothesis there, but σ > 7/8 is already covered by Bourgain, so the new content is nil for the open range) and a Liu follow-up that marginally improves it; Bai's arXiv claim of an unconditional RH proof (5 Mar 2026, withdrawn by its author on 10 Mar 2026; RH would imply the density hypothesis, so this is a claim about the bullet's neighbour, not evidence for it); and a Pintz lecture abstract (11 Nov 2025) whose 'will prove the density hypothesis' sentence is ambiguous with its own narrow-strip history, with no write-up found. Gupta's Oxford talk (25 May 2026) proves a zero-density bound conditional on the Lindelöf hypothesis, which does not settle the unconditional problem. The Claude-credited results (Anthropic 10 Aug 2026; Alpöge–Furman arXiv 13 Aug 2026; Lamzouri 2 Sep 2026; Knausgård 6 Oct 2026) concern the proportion of zeta zeros on the critical line, which is a different quantity from N(σ,T) for σ > 1/2; the record keeps them as events, and their AI attribution is quoted from the authors' own text where it exists (Alpöge–Furman's opening note; Anthropic's post; OpenAI's GitHub page). Close calls: (1) whether the Pintz 2025 lecture claims the full density hypothesis (its abstract supports both readings); (2) whether the OpenAI zero-free half-plane counts as settling the density hypothesis for σ > 7/8 (it does give N = 0 there, but that range was already covered); (3) whether the Alpöge–Furman and Anthropic results should be read as a density-type question at all (I say no, since they bound the proportion of zeros on the line and not N(σ,T)). The parent Lindelöf problem was not researched beyond what the density hypothesis subsection gives; Bourgain's 2017 μ(1/2) = 13/84 and a January 2026 TIFR colloquium claim of GL(2)-based progress on Lindelöf are parent-level and do not bound N(σ,T), so they are not recorded as events.
competing_reading: A reader could count more of the in-window material as bearing on the density hypothesis. (a) OpenAI's zero-free half-plane for ζ, if correct, gives N(σ,T) = 0 for σ above 7/8 (or 11/12), which literally satisfies the statement for those σ; read this way it is the most direct in-window statement about the zeta zeros near the density hypothesis's range, and it is AI-generated per OpenAI. (b) Guth–Maynard's 30/13 is the sup of the very exponent the density hypothesis bounds at 2, so it can be counted as a partial move of the quantity named in the problem rather than a neighbouring result. (c) Pintz's lecture abstract 'will prove the density hypothesis' read at face value would be a major in-window result; read with its own history paragraph it is a strip result. (d) Cheng's 2008 claims, if one ignores the 2021 withdrawal, are a full proof. (e) Bai's withdrawn RH claim implies the density hypothesis if correct. Against all of these: each either leaves the exponent 2 unreached on the open range, is unverified or withdrawn, or concerns a different quantity.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The text of Pintz's November 2025 lecture (or notes): does it prove the density hypothesis for all σ in (1/2,1) or only a strip? (2) The OpenAI manuscripts and any expert verdict: the exact statement of the Lean-checked 7/8 result for ζ (whether it is for all T, and what happens at the excluded principal pole) and whether the 11/12 companion is also checked. (3) Bourgain's 2000 paper: the exact σ range it gives. (4) Guth–Maynard v2 (Apr 2026) changes and whether any A(σ) ≤ 2 range beyond 25/32 is claimed in the Annals version. (5) For Cheng 2008: the withdrawn text and whether any journal accepted it. (6) The full text of Gupta's conditional bound, to check its exponent against 2(1−σ). (7) A written verdict from Conrey or Goldston on the Claude result, if they make one (not needed for the density hypothesis, but it bears on the AI record).

dead_ends: No peer-reviewed or expert-published proof of the density hypothesis was found anywhere in the window; the only full-proof claim is Cheng 2008 (withdrawn 2021).
No AlphaEvolve, Gemini or DeepMind result on zero density or the density hypothesis was found; searches returned only older zero-density literature.
No GPT or Gemini result on the density hypothesis was found; the only 2026 AI results on this topic are Claude's (proportion on the line) and OpenAI's (zero-free half-planes).
No Tao blog post on the Claude result was found in search; not opened from his blog.
The Quanta article on Guth–Maynard was not found in search; the MIT news clip citing it says it reported a 'proof of the Riemann hypothesis', which the papers do not support.
The Conrey and Goldston expert review is reported by Anthropic and secondary coverage only; no statement by either was found.
The Pintz 2025 lecture has no notes, video or preprint in search results; a 2025 arXiv paper by Pintz on the density hypothesis was searched for and not found.
The Preprints.org PDF of the Robles Leyton critique returned HTTP 403; only the prereview.org abstract was read.
The AIM 2026 AI-and-number-theory problem list is a binary PDF that could not be read, so I could not check whether it lists the density hypothesis as open.
Several crank or self-published RH proofs (Zenodo, Mendeley, EasyChair, Cambridge Engage) turned up in searches; none was DH-specific or reviewed, and they are not recorded as events.
Turán's 1954 alternative proof of Lindelöf-implies-density is mentioned in one search summary and not opened.
Wang's follow-ups to Lamzouri (arXiv 2609.24167, 2609.07918, 2609.15329) appeared in search and were not opened; they concern proportions on the line, not the density hypothesis.
Ingham's explicit form (arXiv 2507.15184, July 2025) appeared in search and was not opened; a search summary says it gives explicit constants only, not a new exponent.
Beurling-zeta density results by Pintz and Révész (arXiv 2407.12746) and Broucke are on a different zeta function and were not recorded.
